categories.main_business_segments: Cleveland-Cliffs operates primarily through its Steelmaking segment, which is the largest flat-rolled steel producer in North America. Other business segments include Tubular Components (carbon and stainless steel tubing), Tooling and Stamping (advanced-engineered solutions, tool design, hot- and cold-stamped steel components), and European Operations (trading companies). The company is vertically integrated, controlling the supply chain from mining raw materials to finished steel products.
categories.core_technologies_production_methods: The company utilizes both integrated steelmaking (blast furnace/basic oxygen furnace, BOF) and electric arc furnace (EAF) technologies, supported by internally sourced iron ore pellets, hot briquetted iron (HBI), ferrous scrap, and coking coal. It operates a modern direct reduction plant for HBI, advanced finishing facilities, and maintains a state-of-the-art Research and Innovation Center for product development and process improvement. The company emphasizes advanced high-strength steels (AHSS), electrical steels (GOES/NOES), and environmentally efficient production methods.
categories.primary_customers_markets: Cleveland-Cliffs' primary customers are in the North American automotive industry, where it is the largest supplier of automotive-grade steel. Other key markets include infrastructure and manufacturing (e.g., HVAC, appliances, construction, energy), steel distributors and converters, and other steel producers. In 2022, 31% of revenue came from direct automotive, 26% from infrastructure/manufacturing, 28% from distributors/converters, and 15% from steel producers.
categories.geographic_coverage: The company operates mainly in the United States and Canada, with major steelmaking and finishing facilities across Illinois, Indiana, Michigan, Ohio, Pennsylvania, and West Virginia. It owns or co-owns five active iron ore mines in Minnesota and Michigan, a direct reduction plant in Ohio, scrap processing facilities in the Midwest and Ontario, and a coal mining complex in West Virginia. Sales are principally to North American customers, with some international trading via its European Operations.
categories.supply_chain_position: Cleveland-Cliffs is a vertically integrated steel producer, operating from upstream (mining iron ore and coal) through midstream (direct reduction, scrap processing, coke production) to downstream (primary steelmaking, finishing, stamping, tooling, and tubing). This integration allows the company to control raw material inputs, production, and delivery of finished steel products.
categories.strategic_focus_rd_direction: Strategic priorities include maximizing commercial strengths in high-end markets (especially automotive), leveraging a U.S.-centric and internally sourced supply chain, optimizing the integrated steelmaking footprint, advancing participation in the green economy (EVs, renewable energy, electrical grid modernization), and enhancing environmental sustainability (targeting a 25% reduction in GHG emissions by 2030). R&D focuses on advanced steel grades, electrical steels for EVs, and process innovations to reduce carbon intensity.
categories.revenue_model: The company generates revenue primarily through the sale of steel products (flat-rolled, coated, stainless, electrical, plate, tubular, and stamped components), iron ore pellets, HBI, scrap, and coke. Approximately 45% of flat-rolled steel shipments are sold under annual fixed-price contracts (mainly to automotive customers), with the remainder sold on spot or index-linked pricing. Additional revenue comes from sales to infrastructure, manufacturing, distributors, and other steel producers.
categories.key_competitors_industry_positioning: Major competitors include domestic and foreign producers of flat-rolled steel, EAF-based steelmakers, and alternative material suppliers (e.g., aluminum). Key U.S. competitors are Nucor, U.S. Steel, and Steel Dynamics. Cleveland-Cliffs is the largest flat-rolled steel and automotive steel supplier in North America, with a unique position as the only U.S. producer of both GOES and NOES electrical steels and a fully integrated supply chain. EAF competitors are more exposed to volatile scrap and pig iron markets and have a narrower product range.
categories.financial_scale_growth_profile: In 2022, Cleveland-Cliffs reported record revenues of $23 billion, with Adjusted EBITDA of $3.2 billion and net income of $1.4 billion. The company produced 16.8 million net tons of raw steel and processed 3 million net tons of scrap. It employs approximately 27,000 people. Recent growth has been driven by acquisitions (AK Steel, ArcelorMittal USA, FPT) and expansion into scrap processing and HBI. The company reduced debt by $1.1 billion in 2022 and continues to focus on financial flexibility and operational efficiency.
categories.value_proposition_product_differentiatio: Cleveland-Cliffs differentiates itself through its vertically integrated, U.S.-centric supply chain, comprehensive product portfolio, and leadership in high-end automotive and electrical steels. Its ability to internally source key raw materials provides cost stability and supply security. The company emphasizes superior product quality, technical support, customer service, and innovation, particularly for demanding applications in automotive and the green economy (EVs, renewable energy). Its fixed-price contract structure also provides revenue stability in a volatile industry.
